question:
Batch 89 = the integrator's MERGE AUDIT of branch pp-backtest (383337b4, Nov 12; its session is DONE) into the release line. pp-backtest is a research tool for the retired story-first path: pipeline/oracle/ (a new package: export, lineup, prompts, llm, providers, run, score, witness, ab, replay, report), tests/oracle/, tools/backtest_oracle.py and its docs; additions only (74 files). Nothing in the render path imports pipeline.oracle; it imports pipeline modules flat (canon, editorial_select, punctuation, sentence_law, transcript_store, story_semantics, backtest) after pipeline/oracle/__init__.py puts pipeline/ on sys.path. Its outputs go under --out (default /home/ultron/heimdall_probe/pp_redteam/oracle, outside the repo); its report subcommand writes docs/audits/BACKTEST_SUPPLY_REPORT.md. The branch's own code was audited four rounds on the branch (Gemini / GPT-4o / Grok, a frontier verify, then Heimdall). This audit is of what the MERGE changes and of the merged safety surface.
Two house rules blocked the merge as it stood, and SECTION A of the diff fixes both:
(1) Keys: pipeline/oracle/llm.env_key parsed a hard-coded key-file path (ENV_PATH). The house rule (it held the pp-tests merge, batch 78): every key by NAME through the pipeline's loader, relay.get_key (video_pipeline_v3/relay.py:56, unchanged: the process environment first, then the project's key files; required=False returns '' when missing), the MAIN tree's copy, pinned (never from the environment: that would choose a file to execute in a process holding keys), loaded by file path with importlib (sys.path untouched) and sys.dont_write_bytecode set around the load. Now: KEY_LOADER (llm.py:24), _loader() (llm.py:41, once per process under a lock), env_key(name) (llm.py:59): '' -> KeyError; the value is remembered only for redact(). Callers: providers.available() (a missing key -> the back-end is skipped), _openai_compat, _anthropic, heimdall_usage.
(2) GPU0, law L-r (pipeline/gpu0.py, unchanged: every GPU load holds that GPU's lease; held() :190 is True only while THIS process holds the lease, an inherited lease descriptor counting as custody; current_gpu() :131 is 1 only when CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES == '1', else 0; lease_path() :158 reads PP_GPU<n>_LEASE, default /tmp/pulse_gpu<n>.lease; gpu0.LeaseMissing is a BaseException). The oracle's local back-end (gemma3:27b on GPU0's Ollama, 127.0.0.1:11434) was gated by the environment variable PP_GPU0_LEASE_HELD=1, which any process can set. Now: providers.gpu0_lease_held() (providers.py:190) = gpu0.current_gpu() == 0 and gpu0.held(); available() (providers.py:167, used by call()'s chain walk and by call_backend for every gpu0 back-end, providers.py:274, unchanged) refuses the local back-end without it; _ollama (providers.py:198) itself raises gpu0.LeaseMissing before any request without it (defence in depth for any direct caller). The lease holder (the integrator) makes the model resident; the oracle never swaps models. Default role chains skip the local back-end anyway until its A/B passes (LOCAL_VALIDATED all False); only an explicit chain (the A/B harness) reaches it.
Tests (SECTION A): tests/oracle/conftest.py gives EVERY oracle test its own lease files (PP_GPU0_LEASE / PP_GPU1_LEASE under tmp_path) and CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES '', so no test can touch a render's lease; tests that need the lease hold the REAL gpu0.lease on that file. New: an environment variable never opens the gate, a GPU1 lease never opens it, the real lease does; the real _ollama with a stubbed urlopen: without the lease LeaseMissing and nothing sent, with it one request to the configured host; env_key with every file open denied asks a stubbed loader by name (empty or missing -> KeyError); the real loader loads the main tree's relay.py by path and answers a key set in the environment, sys.path unchanged. One test's expectation follows ruling 93 (no channel is ineligible by name). 177 passed under a network guard (connect / DNS refused); the live lease files untouched (mtimes checked). On the pre-fix code the five new or changed lease / key tests fail (the variable alone opened the gate; _ollama sent without the lease; env_key opened the main tree's key file) and the mirror passes.
FIND, verifying only from the diff and the cited unchanged lines: (a) any remaining way the merged oracle code reads a key other than by name through relay.get_key, or prints, logs or writes a key; (b) any path by which a merged oracle call reaches GPU0's Ollama (or loads a model on a GPU) without this process holding GPU0's lease; (c) any way a test in tests/oracle can touch the live lease files, the network, a paid vendor or the real key files; (d) any effect of the merge on the render path or its services (an import, a sys.path change seen by a run, a shared file written). Reply with the JSON verdict; keep the reasoning short; at most 3 findings, each with file:line and a concrete failure.

consensus_findings.issue: The 'no file is opened here' test patches builtins.open, io.open and os.open, but the real loader path is exercised in a separate test; in the stubbed test, monkeypatch.setattr(llm, "_loader", ...) bypasses _loader entirely, so the test never proves that the REAL _loader's importlib.util.spec_from_file_location/open path avoids the hard-coded ENV_PATH — that proof rests on the second test's inspect.getsourcefile assertion, which pins the absolute path /home/ultron/protocol_pulse/video_pipeline_v3/relay.py and will fail (not skip) on any other checkout, making the suite machine-specific. Concrete failure: running the suite on a checkout not at that literal path fails test_the_real_loader_is_the_main_trees_relay_and_answers_by_name even though the code is correct.
consensus_findings.fix: Compare against llm.KEY_LOADER (the constant the loader actually uses) instead of a second hard-coded literal: assert inspect.getsourcefile(llm._GET_KEY[0]) == llm.KEY_LOADER.

rejected_findings.issue: The once-per-process loader cache is keyed on nothing: if the first _loader() call happens while KEY_LOADER's file is momentarily absent (or fails), the FileNotFoundError propagates, but if a caller catches it and retries, the retry re-executes the whole load under the lock — fine — yet the module is registered in sys.modules as '_pp_oracle_relay' by spec_from_file_location+exec_module only if exec succeeds; a partially executed module (exec_module raising mid-way) leaves no _GET_KEY entry, so a later successful retry would exec a SECOND module object while the first may have already run import-time side effects (relay.py's import-time work) twice in one process.
rejected_findings.evidence:
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("_pp_oracle_relay", KEY_LOADER)
            mod = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
            prev, sys.dont_write_bytecode = sys.dont_write_bytecode, True
            try:
                spec.loader.exec_module(mod)
            finally:
                sys.dont_write_bytecode = prev
            _GET_KEY.append(mod.get_key)
rejected_findings.fix: Register the module in sys.modules before exec (sys.modules[spec.name] = mod) and, on failure, pop it in the finally, so a retry cannot double-execute relay.py's import-time side effects; or catch, clean, and re-raise with the module deregistered.

rejected_findings.issue: The defence-in-depth lease check in _ollama races the lease: gpu0_lease_held() is evaluated once before the request, but nothing keeps this process's lease alive for the duration of the (up to 3600 s) call; if the lease expires mid-call another process may take GPU0 and start its own Ollama work while this call is still streaming — the check proves custody only at send time, not for the call. This is inherent to the design (the integrator holds the lease) and the cited unchanged gpu0.held() semantics, so it is a residual, not a regression.
rejected_findings.evidence:
if not gpu0_lease_held():                      # every caller, not only call_backend's: no lease, never sent
        import gpu0
        raise gpu0.LeaseMissing(f"ollama:{b['model']}: a GPU0 call without the GPU0 lease (law L-r)")
rejected_findings.fix: Document (or enforce, if gpu0 supports it) that the lease must outlive the call; optionally re-check gpu0.held() after the response and mark the row's custody window, so a reply produced after losing the lease is recorded as such.

missed_in_cycle2_unvoted.issue: env_key treats an empty-string key as missing (KeyError), but relay.get_key with required=False returns '' both for 'unset' and for 'set but empty'; a key legitimately stored as empty (e.g. HEIMDALL_API_KEY=) is indistinguishable from unset, and available() then reports '<KEY> not set' — behaviour, not a defect, but the docstring's 'empty is missing' contract now silently diverges from any caller that sets a key to '' to disable a vendor deliberately.
missed_in_cycle2_unvoted.fix: None needed if 'empty == missing' is the intended house semantics; otherwise return the value and let available() decide, or document the equivalence in the docstring.
